root_cause.text: The `imx8mp-blk-ctrl` driver dynamically disables the NOC_HDCP clock (represented by `BIT(11)` in `HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0`) during the power-off sequence of the `IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP` power domain, which can cause a system hang due to a failed NoC ADB400 port power-down handshake.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the dynamic clock control for `IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP` in `imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_on` and `imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_off`, and instead sets `BIT(11)` of `HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0` in `imx8mp_hdmi_power_notifier` to keep the clock always enabled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unnecessary HDCP power domain handling from the HDMI block control power-on sequence.
intent_record.what: Removed the switch case for IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP from the imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_on function.
intent_record.how: Disables the configuration of the HDCP clock control register bit during the HDMI block control power-on sequence.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove incorrect HDCP clock disabling during HDMI block control power-off.
intent_record.what: Removed the switch case for IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP in the imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_off function, which cleared bit 11 of the HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 register.
intent_record.how: Prevents the deactivation of the HDCP clock during the HDMI block control power-off sequence.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add BIT(11) to the HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 register configuration to ensure proper clock initialization in the i.MX8MP HDMI power notifier.
intent_record.what: Added the BIT(11) flag to the bitmask set on the HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 register within the imx8mp_hdmi_power_notifier function.
intent_record.how: Enables an additional clock control bit during the HDMI power state transition to ensure correct hardware clock behavior.

Add BIT(11) to the HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 register configuration to ensure proper clock initialization in the i.MX8MP HDMI power notifier.

relevance_review.reason: The group's intent to remove or modify the HDCP power domain handling directly addresses the vulnerability caused by the power-off sequence of the HDCP power domain, which was disabling the NOC_HDCP clock and causing a system hang.
The group's core intent is to remove the incorrect HDCP clock disabling during HDMI block control power-off, which directly addresses the root cause of the system hang vulnerability.

The group directly addresses the configuration of BIT(11) in the HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 register, which is the exact clock (NOC_HDCP) and register associated with the system hang vulnerability during power state transitions.
